aspects.fertilizer:
**Ridge Planting:**
Broadcast seed and fertilizer after soil preparation, run a plough and planker, and make ridges at 2.5 feet distance using a tractor. Farmers can use a commercial ridger-cum-seeder planter for this method.

**Intercropping in Standing Cotton:**
Cotton crops must be weed-free. Use a seed rate of 3 kg per acre. Irrigate the cotton field in October until water reaches ridge tops. Double broadcast Canola or Raya seed once water settles. Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation. Cut cotton sticks slightly high after cotton harvest ends.

**Irrigated Varieties:**
For Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, AARI Canola, Sarson DGL, and Canzola on average fertility soils, apply 35 kg nitrogen, 30 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potash per acre. At sowing, apply 1.25 bags DAP and 0.5 bag SOP. Alternatively, apply 3.25 bags 18 percent SSP, 0.5 bag urea, and 0.5 bag SOP. A third option is 1 bag nitrophos, 2.25 bags 18 percent SSP, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**Rain-fed Varieties:**
For Barani Star, Chakwal Raya, and Barani Sarson, apply 35 kg nitrogen, 23 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potash per acre. At sowing, apply 1 bag DAP and 0.5 bag SOP. Alternatively, apply 2.5 bags 18 percent SSP, 0.5 bag urea, and 0.5 bag SOP. A third option is 1 bag nitrophos, 1.5 bags 18 percent SSP, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**Application Schedule:**
Determine fertilizer doses using laboratory soil analysis, or follow average fertility recommendations. In rain-fed areas, apply the entire fertilizer dose at sowing. In irrigated areas, apply all phosphorus, all potash, and one-third of the nitrogen at sowing. Split the remaining nitrogen into two equal parts, applying half with the first irrigation and half before flowering. For private company seeds, follow company recommendations.

**Nutrient Management and Substitutes:**
Apply 4 to 5 kg sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to enhance yield and quality. Use ammonium sulphate instead of urea if it is available. Boron application aids flowering and pollination. If SOP is unavailable, use MOP along with 2 kg sulfur per acre.

**Khad Hisab App and Punjab Support:**
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app named Khad Hisab available on Google Play Store. The app calculates balanced fertilizer requirements for Raya with or without a soil test report. Farmers can watch the introductory video in the app or contact their nearest government soil and water testing laboratory.
aspects.harvesting:
Punjab Varieties:
Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, Khanpur Raya, and Canzola are sown across all Punjab from 15 September to 15 October. Their harvest time is 15 February to 31 March. These varieties suit fertile soils and areas with low water resources.
Chakwal Raya is sown in Northern Punjab from 15 September to 15 October. It is sown in Central and Southern Punjab from 1 October to 15 October. Its harvest time is the entire month of March. Chakwal Raya suits loam or light loam soil.

Cotton Intercropping:
Raya can be intercropped in weed-free standing cotton. Use a seed rate of 3 kg per acre. In October, apply water to the cotton field so it rises over the ridges. Double broadcast Raya seed after the water settles. Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation. Cut cotton sticks slightly high after the cotton harvest ends.

Harvesting:
Harvest Raya when leaves turn yellow, 80 percent of pods turn brown, and grains turn reddish. Harvesting early makes seeds weak and reduces oil content. Harvesting late shatters pods, drops seeds, and reduces yield. Keep harvested crop on a raised place to avoid rain damage. Sun-dry the crop for 6 to 10 days before threshing. Threshers are available for separating seed.
A combine harvester is better for large areas. Harvest with a combine harvester when 90 percent or more pods are brown. Adjust the combine harvester screen. Maintain 90,000 plants per acre if using a combine harvester.

Storage:
Ensure Raya seed moisture is 8 percent before storage to prevent mold. Dry seeds make a cracking sound when chewed. Do not mix different varieties during storage. Inspect warehouses regularly for insect attacks. Fumigate stores using 30 to 35 tablets of aluminum phosphide per 1000 cubic feet.

Spraying:
Use flat fan or flood jet nozzles for weed control in Raya. Use hollow cone nozzles for insect control. Bury empty poison bottles in the ground and dispose of cardboard boxes.

Oil Purification:
Extract crude oil using an expeller or kohlu. Heat 5 kg of crude Raya oil to 85 degrees Celsius without boiling. Add 150 grams of finely ground fuller earth or gachni to the hot oil. Stir thoroughly with a spoon for 5 minutes and remove from the stove. Hang a triangular bag made of thick cloth from a stand or charpai over a clean pot. Filter the lukewarm oil through the cloth bag.
aspects.irrigation:
**Cotton Intercropping:**
Ensure the standing cotton crop is free of weeds.
Keep the Canola or Raya seed rate at 3 kg per acre.
Irrigate the cotton field in October so water rises over the ridges.
Perform a double broadcast of Canola or Raya seed after the water settles.
Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation.
Cut cotton sticks slightly high when the cotton crop ends.

**Irrigation Schedule:**
Three to four irrigations are sufficient for Sarson, Raya, and Canola crops.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after germination.
Apply the second irrigation at flowering.
Apply the third irrigation in a light amount near pod formation.
Apply a light irrigation in case of severe frost.
For ridge-sown crops, irrigate according to crop requirement.

**Fertilizer and Pest Management:**
Apply balanced chemical fertilizers according to soil fertility for good Raya yield and quality.
Apply 4 to 5 kg of sulfur per acre with the second irrigation.
Flood 1 liter of Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre with irrigation water to protect Raya from termite attack.

**Weather and Field Management:**
Stay informed of weather forecasts before sowing or applying irrigation.
Pay special attention to irrigation during drought conditions.
Sow the crop at the recommended time.
Take special care of plant protection.
Plant on ridges in high rainfall areas to protect the crop from heavy rain damage and make excess water drainage easy.
aspects.machinery:
**Land preparation and sowing:**
Prepare the land thoroughly and use a laser land leveler for leveling.
Sow in tar wattar moisture conditions.
Sow in rows at a row-to-row distance of 1 to 1.5 feet.
Seed depth must not exceed 1 to 1.5 inches.
A small seed drill is available for sowing and gives very good results.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.

**Ridge planting:**
After preparing the land, broadcast seed and fertilizer.
Run a plow and plank, then make ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor.
A planter called a ridger-cum-seeder is available in the market for this method.

**Harvesting and threshing:**
Place the harvested crop on an elevated spot to protect pods from rain damage.
Dry the harvested crop in the sun for 6 to 10 days before threshing to separate the seed.
Threshers are available for threshing.

**Combine harvesting:**
A combine harvester is better suited if oilseed crops are grown on a large area.
Harvest with a combine harvester when 90 percent or more of the pods turn brown.
Change the sieve of the combine harvester and make proper adjustments.
Maintain a plant population of 90,000 plants per acre if the crop is to be harvested using a combine harvester.

**Spraying machinery and application:**
Before spraying, fill the machine with plain water to test it and determine the required water volume.
Use the recommended water volume to ensure uniform spray application.
Do not stand against the wind direction while spraying.
Do not spray during strong winds.
Avoid repeatedly using poisons from the same chemical group.
Use a flat fan nozzle or a floodjet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest control.
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground and dispose of cardboard cartons.
aspects.other:
Crop management:
Farmers commonly pick greens from the Raya crop.
Picking greens increases the risk of aphid attacks on the crop.
Picking greens reduces crop yield.
A separate area should be allocated for harvesting greens in a crop cultivated for seed.
Allocating a separate area protects the remaining crop from damage.

Weather and climate:
Climate change causes harmful effects on Raya.
Unexpected and excessive rains cause harmful effects on the crop.
Drought causes harmful effects on the crop.
aspects.overview:
**Punjab Statistics:**
In 2020-21, Raya area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
In 2024-25 provisional estimates, area was 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), production was 499.94 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.23 maunds per acre.

**Soil and Field Conditions:**
Well-drained medium to heavy loam soils are suitable.
Highly saline and waterlogged soils are unsuitable.
Raya varieties tolerate high temperatures.
Raya is profitable in sandy soils with limited irrigation in Thal and Cholistan.
In rice zones, clay soils, and high-rainfall areas, ridge sowing saves water and protects against heavy rains.
Adaptive Research Gujranwala trials confirm good yields from ridge sowing after rice harvest.

**Rain-fed Areas:**
Rabi Raya is grown using moisture conserved from summer monsoon rains.
Conserving monsoon rainwater properly increases Rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.

**Chakwal Raya:**
It suits rain-fed areas and is grown for fodder and seed.
It has a strong stem and resists lodging.
It matures uniformly and pods do not shatter when overripe.
It resists diseases and post-germination drought.
Average yield is 18 to 20 maunds per acre.
Seed contains up to 39 percent oil, which is not suitable for edible use.

**Khanpur Raya:**
It produces relatively bold seeds.
Average yield is 18 to 20 maunds per acre, and yield potential reaches 37 maunds per acre.
Seed contains up to 40 percent non-edible oil.

**Super Raya:**
It suits hot regions and resists pod shattering.
Average yield is about 20 maunds per acre, and yield potential is 42 maunds per acre.
Its oil is non-edible.

**AARI Canola:**
It matures in 110 to 120 days.
Average yield is 18 to 20 maunds per acre, and yield potential is 30 maunds per acre.
Seed contains up to 38 percent oil.
The oil is edible, containing 12 percent Omega-3 for heart and blood pressure health.
Pods do not shatter when overripe.
Its meal is fed to milch animals and poultry.
Its short duration makes it suitable for intercropping with sugarcane.

**Cholistan Raya:**
Approved in 2023, it was developed by Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur for hot, sandy Cholistan areas.
Yield potential reaches 40 maunds per acre.
Seed contains up to 38 percent non-edible oil.
It resists pod shattering and diseases.

**Canzola:**
Approved in 2023, it offers good yield and resists pod shattering.
Its oil is not very suitable for edible use.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Management:
Raya resists diseases, pests, and pod shattering.
Treat seed with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram seed with precise water to protect germination.
Separate saag picking areas from seed crops because picking leaves increases aphid attack and lowers yield.
Avoid early sowing.
Rotate crops and destroy plant residues.
Sow on ridges in high rainfall areas.

Termites:
Attacks occur on underground parts in dry weather.
Apply recommended chemical at rauni or flood 1 liter Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre.
In barani areas, broadcast recommended chemical mixed in 15 to 20 kilograms fine soil before sowing and plow.

Tokka:
Attack risk is higher near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum.
Per acre, spray 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Sawfly:
Larvae attack leaves in October and November.
Per acre, spray 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 milliliters Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams Fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug:
Nymphs and adults attack leaves, pods, and shoots in October and November.
Per acre, spray 400 milliliters Abamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams Acephate 75 SP, or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Per acre, spray 80 milliliters Chlorantraniliprole plus Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 milliliters Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Aphid:
Attacks occur from mid-January to late March.
Complete sowing in the first week of October.
Per acre, spray 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 milliliters Clothianidin 20 EC.
Punjab provides free Chrysoperla cards from 11 extension laboratories: Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Diseases:
For white rust, spray 1.25 milliliters Propiconazole or Difenoconazole per liter water.
For Alternaria blight at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rain, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole per liter water.
For downy mildew, spray 5 grams Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium or 6 grams Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil per liter water.
For bacterial stem rot during continuous smog, spray 2.5 milliliters Benzothiazolinone, 1 gram Streptomycin sulphate, or 6 milliliters Kasugamycin per liter water.
For stem rot, treat seed with 1 gram Thiophanate-methyl per kilogram, or spray 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole per liter water.
For plant blight, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 3.5 grams Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin per liter water.
For rust, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 milliliters Propiconazole per liter water.

Spray Guidelines:
Spray only at economic thresholds during evenings.
Use hollow cone nozzles for insect pests and flat fan or floodjet nozzles for weeds.
Wear goggles, gloves, and rubber boots.
Never hoe immediately after spraying.
aspects.sowing:
**Punjab Varieties and Timing:**
Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, Khanpur Raya, and Canzola are sown across all Punjab from 15 September to 15 October.
Harvest time for these varieties is 15 February to 31 March.
They are best suited for fertile soils and areas with low water resources.

**Chakwal Raya:**
In Northern Punjab, Chakwal Raya is sown from 15 September to 15 October.
In Central and Southern Punjab, it is sown from 1 October to 15 October.
Harvesting takes place throughout the month of March.
Loam or light loam soil is suitable for this variety.

**Thal and Cholistan:**
Raya is a profitable crop in Thal and Cholistan where soil is sandy and irrigation resources are severely limited.

**Field Preparation and Sowing:**
Prepare the land thoroughly and level it using a laser land leveler.
Sow in good soil moisture conditions at a seed depth not exceeding 1 to 1.5 inches.
A small seed drill is available and gives good results.
Keep row spacing at 1.5 feet for Barani Star, Chakwal Raya, Khanpur Raya, and Super Raya.
Maintain an acre plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants.
Check temperature and rainfall forecasts before sowing and irrigating.

**Ridge Sowing:**
Ridge sowing is recommended in clay soils, high rainfall areas, and after rice harvest to save water and protect the crop.
Adaptive Research Gujranwala trials show good yields from sowing Raya on ridges after rice harvesting.
After land preparation, broadcast seed and fertilizer, run a plough and planker, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger-cum-seeder planter is available in the market for this method.

**Intercropping in Cotton:**
Intercrop in standing cotton only if the cotton field is weed-free.
Use a seed rate of 3 kg per acre.
In October, irrigate the cotton field until water reaches the top of the ridges.
Double broadcast Raya seed after the water settles.
Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation.
Cut cotton sticks slightly high when the cotton harvest finishes.

**Rainfed Areas:**
Before the monsoon, deep plough empty fields, strengthen bunds, level land, and plough across the slope.
Do not plough after the monsoon season.
Before sowing, plough twice and plank to conserve moisture.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.
Ensure fields are level and weed-free at sowing time.

**Thinning:**
Thinning must be completed before the first irrigation.
Thin the crop when plants develop 4 leaves.
Remove weak and diseased plants, maintaining a plant-to-plant distance of 9 to 12 inches.

**Weed Control:**
For drill and moisture sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours of sowing.

**Pest and Weather Management:**
Complete sowing in the first week of October to protect the crop from Raya aphids.
If aphids attack, spray one of these options per acre: 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20% SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 ml Clothianidin 20 EC.
Manage irrigation carefully during drought.
Sow on ridges in high rainfall areas to reduce crop damage and drain excess water easily.
aspects.varieties:
**Varieties:**
Recommended Raya varieties are Chakwal Raya, Khanpur Raya, Super Raya, AARI Canola, Cholistan Raya, and Canzola. Raya varieties tolerate high temperatures.
Khanpur Raya has relatively bold seeds, an average yield of 18 to 20 maunds per acre, yield potential up to 37 maunds per acre, and oil content up to 40 percent. Its oil is not suitable for edible use.
Super Raya has an average yield of about 20 maunds per acre, yield potential up to 42 maunds per acre, and non-edible oil. It suits hot regions and resists pod shattering at maturity.
Cholistan Raya was developed at RARI Bahawalpur and approved in 2023 for hot, sandy areas of Cholistan. Its yield potential is up to 40 maunds per acre, oil content is up to 38 percent, its oil is non-edible, and it resists shattering and diseases.

**Punjab Cultivation:**
In all Punjab, Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, Khanpur Raya, and Canzola are sown from September 15 to October 15. Harvesting is from February 15 to March 31. These suit fertile soils and low water resources.

**Seed and Sowing:**
Use healthy seed with at least 80 percent germination. Level the land with a laser leveler. Sow into good moisture at a depth of at most 1.5 inches.
In irrigated areas, use 1.5 to 2 kg seed per acre.
In rain-fed areas, use 1.5 to 2.5 kg seed per acre.
In Cholistan, use 3 to 4 kg seed per acre.
Certified seed is available in limited quantities from Punjab Seed Corporation, NARC Islamabad, Raya Department Ayub Research Institute Faisalabad, Raya Research Center Khanpur, RARI Bahawalpur, BARI Chakwal, and registered private companies. Always use Federal Seed Certification Department certified seed.

**Intercropping in Cotton:**
In weed-free standing cotton, irrigate over ridges in October and double broadcast 3 kg seed per acre once water settles. Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation. Cut cotton sticks high after harvest.

**Combine Harvesting:**
For large areas, harvest when 90 percent or more pods turn brown, adjusting the combine harvester sieve. Maintain 90,000 plants per acre.

**Disease Management:**
Treat seed with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg seed without exceeding chemical or water doses.
For stem rot, treat seed with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg seed. Spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water upon disease appearance.
For epidemic blight at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rain, spray before symptoms with Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter. Rotate crops and destroy residue.
For downy mildew, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter.
For plant blight, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter or Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter.
For wilt or collar rot, where seeds rot, plants dry, and root bark cracks, treat seeds, avoid early sowing, remove weeds, and rotate crops.
aspects.weeds:
**Barani areas:**
Deep plow empty fields before the monsoon to conserve rainwater.
Strengthen field bunds, level the land, and plow across slopes.
Do not plow after the monsoon season.
Plow twice and plank before sowing to preserve moisture.
Ensure fields are level and weed-free at sowing time.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.

**Common weeds:**
Prevalent weeds in Raya include Jai, Dumbi sitti, Lashkni booti, Bathu, Karund, Shahtra, and It-sit.

**Non-chemical weed control:**
Use the Dab method after rauni or rain when soil has watter moisture.
Plow, apply heavy planking, and leave the field untouched for 5 to 7 days.
Weeds will emerge and then be destroyed during final seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain.
Complete the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Complete the second hoeing after irrigation once the soil reaches watter condition.
Thin the crop at the four-leaf stage to achieve recommended plant spacing.

**Chemical weed control:**
For pre-emergence weed control, spray Pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre.
In moderate weather at or below 35 degrees Celsius, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill sowing and watter sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
To destroy It-sit emerging within two weeks after crop emergence, spray 400 to 500 ml Metazachlor 50 percent SC per acre.
Metazachlor spray can be applied without using a shield.

**Application equipment and safety:**
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect sprays.
Bury empty chemical bottles underground and destroy cardboard cartons.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after chemical herbicide application.
Hoeing after spray breaks the chemical barrier and allows weeds to regrow.
Hoeing also raises airborne chemical dust that can be inhaled and harm farmer health.

**Wilt disease prevention:**
Wilt causes rotten seeds, plant wilting, drying, and cracked root bark.
Treat seeds with recommended fungicide before planting.
Avoid early sowing, keep the field free of weeds, and practice crop rotation.
